report.summary: Tested "Create a new product and test its input validation" for PROCOL DEMO. Designed 7 test cases across 4 dimensions. Executed 1 flow(s) live, 0 failed (database-verified). Probed the phone field with 4 inputs and found 1 mismatch(es).

findings.title: Phone field accepts non-digit characters (server-side validation gap)
findings.whatHappened: The create-user API accepted a phone value containing letters ("3224962ABC") with HTTP 200. It validates length (rejects 9 or 11 digits) but not that the value is numeric.
findings.likelyCause: Server-side validation checks digit COUNT but not digit TYPE, so it is more lenient than the UI's digits-only rule.
evidence: Live UAT probe: a 10-char value with letters → 200 OK; 9 or 11 digits → 422 'Invalid phone number'.
PRD §5 requires malformed input to be rejected politely.

report.recommendation: Add a digits-only (and length) check to the phone field's server-side validation so the API matches the UI rule, and return a specific error message.

events.reasoning: I searched Procol's own code, config map, endpoint list and PRD for: "Create a new product and test its input validation". Top evidence came from: prd-procol-sourcing.md, console-config-map.md, catalog.json, endpoints.md. The product supports creating multi-stage sourcing events (RFP/RFQ/auction), inviting vendors, and awarding, plus team-based user management. I found one spec-vs-product gap worth testing: the phone field — the PRD says accept any 10-digit number, but the backend only validates length, not digit-type.

deltas.prdSays: Accept any 10-digit number; reject malformed input politely (PRD §4.3, §5).
deltas.productDoes: The API checks phone LENGTH (rejects 9 or 11 digits) but NOT that characters are digits — it accepts a 10-char value containing letters. The frontend enforces digits-only, so the API is more lenient than the UI.
